name: Lobero Theatre

location.text: 33 East Canon Perdido Street, Santa Barbara, California
aliases: 33 E Canon Perdido St, Santa Barbara, California

dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox prints 'Opened February 22, 1873' for the ORIGINAL Lobero opera house on the site and 'Renovated 1922-24' for the building that stands; the article says 'The new Lobero Theatre opened in August 1924. Constructed on the site of the original opera house'. `built` records the George Washington Smith building, not the 1873 house it replaced.

refs.title: Lobero Theatre - Wikipedia
refs.note: 'the building incorporated elements associated with Spanish Colonial Revival architecture, including stucco walls, tiled roofs, arched openings, wrought-iron detailing, and an intimate courtyard-oriented design.' Architects given as George Washington Smith and Lutah Maria Riggs; capacity 604.

refs.title: California Historical Landmark, reference no. 361 (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
PCAD - Smith, George Washington, Architect
refs.note: Carries the contemporary trade record of the second Lobero's plans: '"Lobero Theatre #2 Plans, Santa Barbara", Southwest Builder & Contractor, 42, col 1, 10/26/1923' and '"Lobero Theatre #2, Santa Barbara plans 11/9/1923", Southwest Builder & Contractor, 46, col 2, 11/9/1923.'

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026 as the building that put Smith's manner on a public street a year before the earthquake — the article ties its August 1924 reopening to Santa Barbara's first Old Spanish Days Fiesta and to 'the city's emerging Spanish Colonial Revival identity'. It carries a state landmark number and no National Register number in the source read, and no survey; nothing further is asserted.
